long_biography.plain_text:
Australian entrepreneur Tom Misner maintained a recording career alongside his education business. A musician and recording engineer, he worked with singers including Grace Knight and Tina Martyn. When teaching audio, he favoured learning through studio practice, bringing in other specialists to cover subjects such as electronics and adapting courses to local recording industries.

He took a close personal role in rebuilding Sydney's Studios 301 after buying it back in 2017. Working with acoustician Jochen Veith, he developed the floor plans and chose details down to the light switches. The resulting complex placed recording and mixing rooms near mastering suites, with spaces designed for everything from individual performers to orchestras.

uncertainties.detail: No exact birth date or reliably explicit birth year verified. Age references are not converted into a birth year. Zagreb versus Austrian-born reports conflict; both birthplace candidates remain below threshold. No unsupported middle name, secondary nationality or earned doctorate proposed.

Original real-estate dominance is a medium-confidence inference from explicit personal attribution plus independently documented substantial assets. Current property continuity is positively supported, although the most recent portfolio description is promotional. Neither total transaction values nor global school revenue are personal assets, and personal homes alone do not establish the commercial sector. No audited net worth is asserted.

Maternal restaurant wealth enabled financing and business survival. Her minority equity purchases are distinct from a gift of an established core school or an inherited property fortune. The exact later disposition of her stake is unknown; no family transfer is invented.

Forbes checked first. LinkedIn, Instagram, personal websites, Facebook, Twitter/X, YouTube, TikTok, Wikipedia, company sites, Vimeo, Flickr, Trip Advisor and Zillow reviewed. Instagram tom_misner and Facebook tom.misner were unverified leads without official corroboration. TikTok access was restricted. Third-party Vimeo event videos, son Bobby's YouTube activity and company Wikipedia articles are not personal profiles. No other account meets threshold.

Some social pages were available only in indexed text; direct LinkedIn and Instagram opens failed. The AudioTechnology HTML page timed out, so the designer-hosted full PDF was read. A misleading technology-finance biography and unrelated American property agents were excluded. Hermitage's automatically associated wine-business listing was not accepted as his company.

Biographies omit vessels, disputed birthplace, promotional net-worth numbers and private health information. Studio ownership is not described as continuous through the period around the SAE disposal. Only three active tags are assigned, with separate educational, property and professional dimensions; no taxonomy candidates or shared edits.

The 2025 publisher describes time divided between Australia and Europe; it does not specify Monaco. Independent 2018 reporting identifies Monaco residence historically. No relative main-base change is established; existing Australia residence remains untouched and no optional residence field is proposed.
